chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Chicago vacation, the Savoy and the Arcadia offer (second version)
summary: No Chicago or Detroit jobs; they play the Savoy; Meyer Davis wanted them at the Arcadia but Trent chose Cleveland.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Let's see, from Canada you come down--I guess from Canada you must have come down to Cleveland; you never did play in Chicago; did you?
No, we didn't play in Chicago at all. We had a vacation and went to Chicago--all of us went to Chicago.
You just had a vacation in Chicago; that's right, because you would have been right across the river. You didn't play Detroit either, did you?
Didn't you play New York around this time? Didn't you play the Arcadia?
No, we came and played the Savoy.
You had the opportunity, you could have gone--

Meyer Davis wanted to put us in the Arcadia, but the Arcadia was the number two ballroom in New York at that time. Roseland was the number one ballroom but in those days Roseland and the Arcadia were real jobs. We had the opportunity of going and staying in New York and playing the Arcadia or going to Cleveland and playing the Plantation. The reason that prevailed upon everybody to take the job in Cleveland, he was afraid different bands in New York would steal the different men. I know I had a couple of offers to go to different bands.
I'd think you probably would; sure.
Yes, I did. Some of the other guys got offers--
